back2basics.text: Midterm elections in the U.S. occur every four years, halfway through a president's term, to elect members of Congress including the entire House of Representatives and one-third of the Senate. These elections can change the balance of power in Congress, affecting the president's ability to pass legislation and shape policy.

back2basics.text: Nuclear reactors generate heat that must be continuously removed to prevent overheating and potential meltdown. This cooling requires a reliable power supply to operate pumps and safety systems. External power is critical because nuclear plants often do not generate electricity for their own cooling needs, relying instead on external grids or backup generators to maintain safe conditions.

2026-11-09-am-70bf0e5418.deck: The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine lost its external electricity supply on November 8, 2026, forcing it to depend on emergency diesel generators to keep its nuclear fuel cool. This situation highlights the nuclear safety risks in conflict zones, relevant for understanding international security and environmental concerns.

back2basics.text: Naxalism refers to armed insurgency movements inspired by Maoist ideology, primarily active in certain forested and rural areas of India. The government combats Naxalism through security operations, cutting funding and supply lines, and development initiatives to win local support.

back2basics.concept: Air Quality Index (AQI) and PM2.5 pollution
back2basics.text: The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a measure that indicates how polluted the air is on a given day, with categories ranging from 'good' to 'severe'. PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less, which can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream, posing serious health risks. Monitoring AQI and PM2.5 helps assess pollution levels and inform public health advisories.

2026-11-09-am-a36157808b.deck: During Deepavali 2026, Delhi experienced air pollution levels over 50 times the WHO limit as many residents ignored the Supreme Court's firecracker restrictions. This highlights challenges in enforcing environmental regulations and managing urban pollution, important for understanding governance and public health issues.

body.label: Firecracker use despite ban
body.text: Many Delhi residents burst traditional firecrackers beyond the Supreme Court's 10 p.m. deadline and green cracker restrictions, contributing heavily to pollution spikes.

body.label: High PM2.5 concentrations

body.text: Winter meteorological conditions, stubble burning in October-November, vehicle emissions, and dust also worsened air quality during this period.

body.text: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) can penetrate deep into lungs and bloodstream, causing respiratory and cardiovascular problems, especially in vulnerable populations.
